newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best affirms rating of Prudential's N.J. unit.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best affirms rating of Prudential's N.J. unit.

text.p: A.M. Best said it affirmed the A- rating claims-paying ability of Prudential Property and Casualty Insurance Co of New Jersey, but said it revised its rating outlook downward to negative.
The New Jersey unit is a sister affiliate of Prudential Property and Casualty Insurance Co, which was earlier downgraded by A.M. Best to B++ from A-.

The New Jersey outfit's rating affirmation reflects its strong local market presence, good capitalization and historically strong underwriting results, with a five-year combined ratio of 104, a measure of profitability.
It also reflects the favorable implications of a dedicated management team recently committed to the New Jersey marketplace, A.M. Best said.
These positive rating factors are offset by PRUPAC of New Jersey's unfavorable spread of risk, A.M. Best said.
A.M. Best said PRUPAC of New Jersey's catastrophe exposures remain high relative to catastrophe leverage standards for Excellent-rated carriers.
In addition, A.M. Best cited its business concentration in New Jersey, a historically unfavorable regulatory environment for personal lines carriers.
The company also has experienced a general downturn in its underwriting results during 1996, A.M. Best said.
Therefore, A.M. Best said, the company's rating outlook is negative.
PRUPAC of New Jersey, with $539 million in net writings and $306 million of surplus at year-end 1995, ranks among the top three personal lines carriers in New Jersey.
